statement: Write freq(v) for the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. A multiset S drawn from nums means that for every integer v, the number of copies of v in S is at most freq(v). Say S is pattern-valid if there exist an integer x >= 1 and an integer q >= 0 such that either (i) x = 1 and S consists of exactly 2*q+1 copies of 1, or (ii) x > 1 and S consists of exactly two copies of x^(2^j) for each j with 0 <= j < q, exactly one copy of x^(2^q), and no other elements. For q = 0 this means one copy of x; the case q >= 1 matches the required pattern with k = 2^q. Then the function returns a result r, and r is the maximum of |S| over all pattern-valid multisets S drawn from nums.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, or signal integer overflow or out-of-bounds access.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 1 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is odd; that is, r = 2*q+1 for some integer q >= 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: If there is an integer v such that nums[i] = v for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), then: when v = 1, the returned value r equals len(nums) if len(nums) is odd and equals len(nums)-1 if len(nums) is even; when v > 1, r = 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let freq(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if freq(1) < 3 and, for every integer x >= 2 with freq(x) >= 2, freq(x*x) = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let freq(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v, and let c = freq(1). If c > 0, then the returned value r is at least the largest odd integer not exceeding c; explicitly, r >= c when c is odd and r >= c-1 when c is even.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let freq(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. For every integer x >= 2 and every integer q >= 0 such that freq(x^(2^j)) >= 2 for all integers j with 0 <= j < q and freq(x^(2^q)) >= 1, the returned value r satisfies r >= 2*q+1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let freq(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. There exist an integer x >= 1 with freq(x) > 0 and an integer q >= 0 such that the returned value r satisfies r = 2*q+1 and either (x = 1 and freq(1) >= r), or (x >= 2, freq(x^(2^j)) >= 2 for all j with 0 <= j < q, and freq(x^(2^q)) >= 1).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let freq(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. If freq(1) = 0, then the returned value r equals the maximum, over all integers x >= 2 with freq(x) > 0, of 2*Q(x)+1, where Q(x) is the largest integer q >= 0 such that freq(x^(2^j)) >= 2 for all j with 0 <= j < q and freq(x^(2^q)) >= 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let r be the result returned for nums. For every slice nums' of 64-bit integers with len(nums') = len(nums) and, for every integer v, the number of indices i with nums'[i] = v equals the number of indices i with nums[i] = v, if the function returns r' on nums', then r' = r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let nums' be any slice obtained from nums by appending one extra integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000000000, and assume len(nums)+1 <= 100000. If the function returns r on nums and r' on nums', then r' >= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let freq(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer x >= 1 and every integer q >= 0, if either (i) x = 1 and freq(1) >= 2*q+1, or (ii) x >= 2 and freq(x^(2^j)) >= 2 for all integers j with 0 <= j < q and freq(x^(2^q)) >= 1, then 2*q+1 <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let freq(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 3, either freq(1) >= 3 or there exists an integer x >= 2 such that freq(x) >= 2 and freq(x*x) >= 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.
